# doc_baseline.txt -- the documentation ratchet: findings of zl lint --docs-all per
# (rule, file). A count may only go DOWN; lower a row as the docs are written, delete it
# at zero. ztestrunner's doc kind enforces it, under --heavy (make ci) only -- it is a
# full-corpus lint pass, too slow for the fast gate.
#
# The codes: L016 an undocumented definition, L017 an undocumented parameter, L018 an
# undocumented member (a record/class field, a variant/union arm, or a generic
# parameter), L024 a doc that only re-says the declaration below it, L025 a doc body
# repeated more than twice in one file.
#
# THE TARGET IS ZERO for every row in lib/system/, which is the public API surface and
# takes the universal bar. That includes zast.z, zlexer.z, zparser.z and zvfs.z: they are
# the compiler's front end rather than stdlib anyone imports, but they live here and are
# read the same way, so they are held to the same standard.
#
# THE TARGET IS ZERO for L016, L018, L024 and L025 in src/, on a judgment bar: a comment
# must add something the name and the type cannot, and where nothing can be added the
# answer is to rename the member, not to write filler.
#
# L017 IN src/ IS NOT A ZERO TARGET -- it ratchets downward and nothing more. L017 fires
# only on a parameter that starts its own source line, and `zl fmt --line-length 100` has
# already exploded roughly 1,260 parameter lists in src/ FOR WIDTH, not for explanation,
# putting thousands of parameters into the rule's scope that nobody chose to explain. The
# rule for new code stands: explode a parameter list only when at least one parameter
# needs explaining. These rows record a debt that was created mechanically, so they come
# down as files are worked and are never expected to reach zero.
